english.title: Resist / obstruct enforcement officer / person acting for engaged to execute High Court writ - Criminal Law Act 1977
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..)

(A)_[resisted]_
(B)_[intentionally obstructed]_

(C)_[an enforcement officer]_
(D)_[a person acting under the authority of an enforcement officer]_

who was engaged in executing a writ issued from the High Court
english.legislation: Contrary to section 10(A1) and (4) of the Criminal Law Act 1977.
english.pointstoprove:
resisted/intentionally obstructed
enforcement officer/person acting under authority of enforcement officer
who was engaged in executing writ from High Court

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Enforcement officer means a person who is authorised to act as an enforcement officer under the Courts Act 2003.
(ii) The offence was added by paragraph 189 of Schedule 8 to the Court Act 2003

other.powersofarrest: A constable in uniform or any officer of a court may arrest without warrant anyone who is, or whom he, with reasonable cause, suspects to be guilty of an offence under this section (Subsection 10(5)).
other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Six months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
